problem: "Size is the outline measured against the image scale" repeats the word "outline" already used for shape, so the student may think size and shape are the same element. Size is the measured extent of the object, not its outline.
fix: "Size is how large the object appears on the image, converted to ground length or area with the scale; it separates a house from a shed."

problem: "Measure several known distances and average them if the photo is tilted" is misleading. On a tilted photo the scale changes from place to place, so a single averaged scale is wrong at most points; averaging only smooths random measurement error on a near-vertical photo.
fix: "On a near-vertical photo, measure several known distances and average them to reduce measurement error. On a tilted photo the scale varies across the frame, so compute the scale for the line or patch you are measuring, or use rectified imagery."

problem: The second node is labelled "Shape, size, shadow" but the aria description says "then shape and shadow", so screen-reader users lose the size element that the visible figure shows.
fix: Change the aria text to "... then shape, size and shadow, then pattern and texture ..." so it matches the node labels.

problem: "Confirm the class from the sun-facing side" is vague. Shadows fall on the side away from the sun, and the interpreter should read the lit side of the object, not a "sun-facing" side.
fix: "Shadow is not a dark surface. It hides the ground it falls on, so read the class from the lit side of the object, or from an image of another date."
